# Command reference

<!-- Generated by docs/gen_cli.py. Do not edit by hand: run `python docs/gen_cli.py` and commit the result. -->

This page is generated from each command's `--help` output by `docs/gen_cli.py`. It keeps the usage line, the first line of the description and the arguments. Run the command with `--help` for the full description.

Every command also runs as `python -m <module>`; the module for each is in `[project.scripts]` in `pyproject.toml`.

## `slens-collect`

Collect comments from YouTube videos into the shared CSV schema.

```text
usage: slens-collect [-h] --story STORY [--search QUERY] [--top-n TOP_N]
                     [--target-videos TARGET_VIDEOS] [--drop-non-lang]
                     [--max-shorts-seconds MAX_SHORTS_SECONDS] [--min-comments MIN_COMMENTS]
                     [--seed SEED] [--limit LIMIT] [--max-search-pages MAX_SEARCH_PAGES]
                     [--order {relevance,time}] [--lang LANG] [--output OUTPUT]
                     [--video-list-output VIDEO_LIST_OUTPUT]
                     [--exclusion-table-output EXCLUSION_TABLE_OUTPUT]
                     [urls ...]

positional arguments:
  urls                  One or more video URLs (preferred)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --story STORY         Short story label, e.g. luigi / elon
  --search QUERY        Search term instead of URLs; repeatable. Each query contributes candidates
                        to one shared pool, deduplicated by video ID, and the hybrid draw happens
                        once over that pool. Repeat it when a story is discussed under several
                        names: the Oxfam inequality report is covered under 'Davos', 'world's
                        richest 1%' and 'wealth gap' without ever being named, and a single query
                        found only 5 videos clearing --min-comments against 25 for Luigi. Five
                        videos is too few for a clustered interval to mean anything, so this is a
                        sample-size fix, not a convenience.
  --top-n TOP_N         Hybrid video selection: take this many videos by relevance first (default
                        10), then fill up to --target-videos at random. See the design-effect note
                        on search_youtube() for why this isn't pure relevance or pure random.
  --target-videos TARGET_VIDEOS
                        Total videos to select per story when using --search (default 30): --top-n
                        by relevance, the rest at random. Precision comes from the number of
                        videos collected, not the number of comments, so this -- not a comment-
                        count target -- is the lever that actually narrows a reported proportion's
                        interval.
  --drop-non-lang       Actually discard comments whose detected language differs from --lang,
                        instead of only recording it. Off by default and worth leaving off:
                        measured over 313 comments this removed 8 and all 8 were English (see
                        #23). The detected_lang column is written either way, so filtering
                        downstream stays reversible.
  --max-shorts-seconds MAX_SHORTS_SECONDS
                        Exclude --search results at or under this many seconds as YouTube Shorts
                        (0 = keep everything). The Data API exposes no authoritative is-a-Short
                        flag, so this is a duration heuristic. Default 60 is deliberately
                        conservative; 180 is the current maximum Shorts length and excludes far
                        more, including short clips from credible channels. Measured on 50 results
                        for 'billionaire wealth tax': 12 videos at or under 60s, 27 at or under
                        180s. Record whichever value was used.
  --min-comments MIN_COMMENTS
                        Only consider search results with MORE than this many comments (soft-
                        coded: raise it to demand a bigger comment section before a video is
                        eligible to be sampled).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for --search video sampling, so the same search reproduces the
                        same picked videos.
  --limit LIMIT         Max top-level comments per video (0 = all). Replies do not count against
                        this.
  --max-search-pages MAX_SEARCH_PAGES
                        How many 50-result pages of search results to walk per --search query
                        (default 1). One page used to be a hard limit, so the candidate pool was
                        the top 50 by relevance and any shortfall was reported as if it were a
                        property of the corpus. Raising this widens the pool, but each page costs
                        100 quota units, and because --seed draws from the pool, a different value
                        produces a DIFFERENT video set for the same seed. Do not change it midway
                        through a collection you intend to reproduce.
  --order {relevance,time}
                        Comment order within each video. Only matters if --limit actually cuts a
                        video's comments short: with every comment collected (--limit 0), the
                        final rows are the same either way. 'time' is the unbiased ordering if a
                        cap does bite; 'relevance' is YouTube's engagement ranking.
  --lang LANG           Keep only comments detected as this ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. 'en'.
                        Requires `pip install langdetect`. Unset (default): no filtering. Comments
                        under ~20 characters are always kept, since a detector cannot trust that
                        little text.
  --output OUTPUT       CSV file to write to. If omitted, writes to stdout (NOT recommended on
                        Windows PowerShell — its '>' redirection re-encodes text as UTF-16, not
                        UTF-8).
  --video-list-output VIDEO_LIST_OUTPUT
                        Write the video-list appendix (video ID, comments kept, dates, search
                        query) to this CSV -- the reproducibility record of exactly which videos
                        went into the corpus.
  --exclusion-table-output EXCLUSION_TABLE_OUTPUT
                        Write the exclusion-accounting table (API-returned vs. removed at each
                        filtering stage) to this CSV, alongside printing it to stderr.
```

## `slens-merge`

Concatenate per-video/per-thread collector CSVs into one master file.

```text
usage: slens-merge [-h] --output OUTPUT [--no-manifest] [--cap-scope {global,story}]
                   [--cap-per-author CAP_PER_AUTHOR] [--dedupe-bodies]
                   inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  inputs                Per-video/per-thread CSVs to combine

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT       Path to write the combined CSV
  --no-manifest         Skip writing the .manifest.json that freezes this corpus. Only for a
                        throwaway file you do not intend to analyse.
  --cap-scope {global,story}
                        --cap-per-author: count an author's comments across all stories (global,
                        the default and what built the frozen corpus) or within each story.
                        'story' makes the result independent of merge order.
  --cap-per-author CAP_PER_AUTHOR
                        Keep at most this many comments per author_hash (see cap_per_author's
                        docstring for why). Off by default: a plain `slens-merge` with no flags
                        reproduces exactly what it always did.
  --dedupe-bodies       Also drop rows whose comment body duplicates an earlier one IN THE SAME
                        STORY (see drop_duplicate_bodies's docstring). Off by default, same
                        reasoning as --cap-per-author.
```

## `slens-clean-videos`

Drop every comment belonging to a named list of videos from a collected comments CSV, before merging.

```text
usage: slens-clean-videos [-h] [--exclude EXCLUDE] [--exclude-file EXCLUDE_FILE] --output OUTPUT
                          input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --exclude EXCLUDE     Comma-separated video IDs to drop
  --exclude-file EXCLUDE_FILE
                        Text file, one video ID per line
  --output OUTPUT
```

## `slens-redact`

Find, and optionally remove, personal identifiers in comment text.

```text
usage: slens-redact [-h] [--output OUTPUT] [--column COLUMN] [--handles {keep,leading,all}]
                    [--handle-token HANDLE_TOKEN] [--emails] [--phones]
                    input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT       Write the redacted corpus here. Without it, only report.
  --column COLUMN
  --handles {keep,leading,all}
  --handle-token HANDLE_TOKEN
  --emails
  --phones
```

## `slens-gemma`

Label comments for harm domain AND sentiment with one model only: Gemma 2 27B Instruct (Q4_0), run locally through Ollama. Nothing leaves the machine.

```text
usage: slens-gemma [-h] [--output OUTPUT] [--check] [--sample N] [--seed SEED] [--limit LIMIT]
                   [--project-to N] [--cache CACHE] [--no-cache] [--keep-empty-cached-replies]
                   [--fixed-examples FILE] [--story-rules {on,off}]
                   [--stance-object {conduct,wealth}] [--sentiment-examples {on,off}]
                   [--domain-context {facts,none}] [--combined-domain-context {keep,remove}]
                   [--host HOST]
                   [input_csv]

positional arguments:
  input_csv             A CSV with a `body` column (and `story`).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT       Where to write the labelled CSV (required to label).
  --check               Check the setup and send two invented comments through the model, then
                        stop.
  --sample N            Label N comments drawn at random, spread evenly across stories. Use this,
                        not --limit, on the corpus file (which is ordered by story).
  --seed SEED           Which random draw --sample makes (default 42). Same seed, same comments.
  --limit LIMIT         Only label the first N comments of the file, in file order.
  --project-to N        After the run, project how long N comments would take from the measured
                        speed.
  --cache CACHE         JSONL response cache (default data/gemma_cache.jsonl). It is what makes a
                        stopped run resumable and this arm reproducible; keep it.
  --no-cache            Do not cache replies. Only for a throwaway trial.
  --keep-empty-cached-replies
                        Proceed although the cache holds empty replies (default: refuse).
  --host HOST           Ollama server address if it is not on this machine (sets OLLAMA_HOST),
                        e.g. http://192.168.1.20:11434.

instrument switches (defaults reproduce the current wording):
  --fixed-examples FILE
                        CSV (comment_id, body, label) of the examples shown to the model in the
                        `fixed` arm, instead of the built-in synthetic set. For real hand-coded
                        gold comments: keep the file in a gitignored folder. They are left out of
                        scoring automatically (each would be scored against its own label), and
                        run records and the dashboard codebook hold their ids and a hash, never
                        their text.
  --story-rules {on,off}
                        off = story context is factual only, with no stance rules
  --stance-object {conduct,wealth}
                        wealth = anchor 4 is about extreme wealth and those who hold it
  --sentiment-examples {on,off}
                        off = the sentiment prompt shows no worked examples. With --fixed-examples
                        FILE holding `sentiment` and `story` columns, on (default) shows the same
                        fixed examples with their ratings
  --domain-context {facts,none}
                        none = the domain prompt carries no story background (the earlier
                        wording); facts (default) = it ends with the story's factual paragraph,
                        never the stance rules
  --combined-domain-context {keep,remove}
                        remove = the combined arm's domain question does not see the story context
```

## `slens-batches`

Split a corpus into batches for a slow local model, and check the labelled batches came back complete and consistent before joining them.

```text
usage: slens-batches [-h] {prepare,verify,split,status,commands,check} ...

positional arguments:
  {prepare,verify,split,status,commands,check}
    prepare             write the full corpus minus the gold/example comments (no spreadsheet
                        involved), with a provenance file
    verify              check a corpus is exactly the full corpus minus the excluded comments,
                        with every text unchanged
    split               cut a corpus into batches
    status              which batches are done, pending or need attention
    commands            print the slens-gemma command for every pending batch
    check               verify finished batches; optionally join them

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `slens-batches prepare`

```text
usage: slens-batches prepare [-h] --exclude FILE --output OUTPUT full_csv

positional arguments:
  full_csv

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --exclude FILE   a file with a comment_id column whose comments are left out (repeatable)
  --output OUTPUT
```

### `slens-batches verify`

```text
usage: slens-batches verify [-h] --full FULL [--exclude FILE] input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit
  --full FULL
  --exclude FILE
```

### `slens-batches split`

```text
usage: slens-batches split [-h] [--full FILE] [--exclude FILE] --out-dir OUT_DIR
                           [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--shuffle-seed SHUFFLE_SEED] [--no-shuffle]
                           input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --full FILE           check the corpus against the full corpus before splitting (with
                        --exclude): refuses a corpus that is not the full corpus minus the
                        excluded comments
  --exclude FILE        with --full: a file whose comment_ids should be absent (repeatable)
  --out-dir OUT_DIR
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
                        comments per batch (default 1,000: about 40 minutes at 2.4 s a comment)
  --shuffle-seed SHUFFLE_SEED
                        seed for the shuffle (default 7)
  --no-shuffle          keep the corpus file's order (batches are then contiguous slices)
```

### `slens-batches status`

```text
usage: slens-batches status [-h] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `slens-batches commands`

```text
usage: slens-batches commands [-h] [--extra EXTRA] [--cache CACHE] [--first N] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --extra EXTRA  flags added to every command, e.g. "--fixed-examples official-data/fixed.csv"
  --cache CACHE  one shared response cache (default <out_dir>/gemma_cache.jsonl)
  --first N      print only the first N batches still to run, in order (e.g. 5 for batches 1 to
                 5); run again later for the next N
```

### `slens-batches check`

```text
usage: slens-batches check [-h] [--merge-to FILE] [--partial] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --merge-to FILE  write the joined, labelled corpus here once every batch is done and checks out
  --partial        with --merge-to: join only the batches finished so far, into a progress file
                   whose run record is marked partial (never the whole corpus)
```

## `slens-anthropic-batch`

Label a corpus with Claude through Anthropic's Message Batches API (half price, slower).

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch [-h] {plan,submit,status,fetch,replay,compare} ...

positional arguments:
  {plan,submit,status,fetch,replay,compare}
    plan                dry run: counts and an estimated cost; sends nothing
    submit              send the missing requests as batches
    status              progress of the batches; --check-cache counts gaps
    fetch               download finished batches into the cache
    replay              label the corpus from the cache alone
    compare             how far two labelled files agree, comment by comment

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `slens-anthropic-batch plan`

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch plan [-h] [--out-dir OUT_DIR] [--judge JUDGE] [--sentiment SENTIMENT]
                                  [--votes VOTES] [--ttl {5m,1h}] [--cache CACHE] [--sample N]
                                  [--seed SEED] [--limit LIMIT]
                                  [--max-batch-requests MAX_BATCH_REQUESTS]
                                  [--max-batch-mb MAX_BATCH_MB] [--retry-uncacheable]
                                  [--fixed-examples FILE] [--story-rules {on,off}]
                                  [--stance-object {conduct,wealth}]
                                  [--sentiment-examples {on,off}] [--domain-context {facts,none}]
                                  [--combined-domain-context {keep,remove}]
                                  input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out-dir OUT_DIR
  --judge JUDGE         the model, as anthropic:<model>
  --sentiment SENTIMENT
                        default llm:<the same model as --judge>
  --votes VOTES
  --ttl {5m,1h}         prompt-cache lifetime on the batch requests. 1h (default) is what
                        Anthropic suggests for batches; 5m is the live default. Cache writes cost
                        2x the input price at 1h, 1.25x at 5m.
  --cache CACHE         response cache (default <out-dir>/batch_cache.jsonl). Use a SEPARATE file
                        from any live run.
  --sample N            only N comments, spread evenly across stories (use this, not --limit, on
                        the corpus file)
  --seed SEED
  --limit LIMIT         only the first N comments (one story, on the corpus)
  --max-batch-requests MAX_BATCH_REQUESTS
  --max-batch-mb MAX_BATCH_MB
  --retry-uncacheable   send again the replies that came back refused or cut off (by default they
                        are used as the live path uses them, not re-bought)

instrument switches (defaults reproduce the current wording):
  --fixed-examples FILE
                        CSV (comment_id, body, label) of the examples shown to the model in the
                        `fixed` arm, instead of the built-in synthetic set. For real hand-coded
                        gold comments: keep the file in a gitignored folder. They are left out of
                        scoring automatically (each would be scored against its own label), and
                        run records and the dashboard codebook hold their ids and a hash, never
                        their text.
  --story-rules {on,off}
                        off = story context is factual only, with no stance rules
  --stance-object {conduct,wealth}
                        wealth = anchor 4 is about extreme wealth and those who hold it
  --sentiment-examples {on,off}
                        off = the sentiment prompt shows no worked examples. With --fixed-examples
                        FILE holding `sentiment` and `story` columns, on (default) shows the same
                        fixed examples with their ratings
  --domain-context {facts,none}
                        none = the domain prompt carries no story background (the earlier
                        wording); facts (default) = it ends with the story's factual paragraph,
                        never the stance rules
  --combined-domain-context {keep,remove}
                        remove = the combined arm's domain question does not see the story context
```

### `slens-anthropic-batch status`

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch status [-h] [--check-cache] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --check-cache
```

### `slens-anthropic-batch fetch`

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch fetch [-h] [--refetch] [--abandon BATCH_ID] [--cancel] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help          show this help message and exit
  --refetch           fetch batches already fetched
  --abandon BATCH_ID  give up on a batch that can never be fetched (its results are gone): its
                      requests become gaps that the next submit sends again. Only a batch that has
                      ended (or no longer exists)
  --cancel            with --abandon on a batch still running: cancel it instead
```

### `slens-anthropic-batch replay`

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch replay [-h] --output OUTPUT [--partial] out_dir

positional arguments:
  out_dir

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT
  --partial        write the complete comments even if some are missing a reply
```

### `slens-anthropic-batch compare`

```text
usage: slens-anthropic-batch compare [-h] file_a file_b

positional arguments:
  file_a
  file_b

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

## `slens-primary-category`

Add a `primary_category` column to a keyword-labelled corpus, for use as a gold-set stratification key: `slens-validate sample --stratify-by story,primary_category`.

```text
usage: slens-primary-category [-h] --output OUTPUT input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT
```

## `slens-adjudicate`

Adjudicate comments coded by exactly three coders, by majority; flag what the majority cannot settle.

```text
usage: slens-adjudicate [-h] --core-ids CORE_IDS [--review-output REVIEW_OUTPUT]
                        [--decisions DECISIONS] [--output OUTPUT] [--gold GOLD]
                        [--gold-output GOLD_OUTPUT] [--sentiment-rule {bucket,exact}]
                        [--extra-labels {add,ignore}]
                        inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  inputs                each coder's ORIGINAL completed file (.xlsx or .csv), exactly three

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --core-ids CORE_IDS   the comment_ids all coders coded
  --review-output REVIEW_OUTPUT
                        step 1: the flagged comments, with the text and every coder's answer, for
                        you to decide
  --decisions DECISIONS
                        step 2: the review file with hand_domain and hand_sentiment filled in for
                        the flagged rows
  --output OUTPUT       the resolved core rows (comment_id, hand_domain, hand_sentiment, ...);
                        written only when nothing remains flagged. `slens-validate combine
                        --adjudicated` reads this
  --gold GOLD           a gold file to copy with the adjudicated labels put in
  --gold-output GOLD_OUTPUT
                        where to write that copy
  --sentiment-rule {bucket,exact}
  --extra-labels {add,ignore}
                        ignore (default): a category only one coder tagged is not added. add: it
                        is added beside the majority label when that makes at most two labels
```

## `slens-classify`

Label each comment with a sentiment score and an LLM harm domain.

```text
usage: slens-classify [-h] [--judge JUDGE] [--selector SELECTOR] [--pool POOL] [--k K]
                      [--seed SEED] [--votes VOTES] [--fuzzy] [--cache-only]
                      [--keep-empty-cached-replies] [--cache CACHE] [--no-cache]
                      [--label-column LABEL_COLUMN] [--concurrency CONCURRENCY] [--strict-corpus]
                      [--limit LIMIT] [--max-cost USD] [--project-to N] [--sentiment SENTIMENT]
                      [--output OUTPUT] [--fixed-examples FILE] [--story-rules {on,off}]
                      [--stance-object {conduct,wealth}] [--sentiment-examples {on,off}]
                      [--domain-context {facts,none}] [--combined-domain-context {keep,remove}]
                      input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --judge JUDGE         '<backend>:<model>'. Backends: anthropic, combined, gemma, google,
                        keyword, manual, ollama, openai, stub. The 1b model used in the pilot was
                        too small to hold four categories apart; prefer 12b or larger.
  --selector SELECTOR   Few-shot examples: fixed, fixed_random, none, retrieved
  --pool POOL           Hand-coded CSV to retrieve examples from
  --k K                 Examples to retrieve (--selector retrieved), or to draw (--selector
                        fixed_random).
  --seed SEED           --selector fixed_random only: which random N-example draw to freeze for
                        the whole run. Same seed always picks the same examples from a given pool.
  --votes VOTES         Samples per comment; labels need a majority to be kept.
  --fuzzy               Restore the old behaviour of fuzzy-matching off-list answers.
  --cache-only          Never call the model: use only replies already in --cache, and stop at the
                        first comment that has none. For replaying answers collected by slens-
                        anthropic-batch, so a gap can never become a full-price call.
  --keep-empty-cached-replies
                        Proceed although the cache holds empty replies (default: refuse).
  --cache CACHE         JSONL response cache, on by default. A long run meets transient failures;
                        with a cache a restart replays completed calls for free and only pays for
                        what is left. Without one, a crash at hour three of a four-hour run loses
                        every call. --no-cache disables it.
  --no-cache            Disable the response cache. Only sensible for a one-off trial run you do
                        not intend to repeat.
  --label-column LABEL_COLUMN
  --concurrency CONCURRENCY
                        How many comments to label at once. The wall-clock cost of an API run is
                        almost entirely waiting on the network, so this is the difference between
                        a run measured in hours and one measured in minutes: 10,000 comments at 3
                        votes is ~33h sequentially and roughly 33/N with --concurrency N. Output
                        row order is unchanged. Keep it at 1 for a local ollama judge, which is
                        compute-bound rather than network-bound and gains nothing.
  --strict-corpus       Refuse to run if the corpus no longer matches the manifest slens-merge
                        wrote. Worth setting for any run whose labels get quoted: a corpus that
                        changed after a figure was produced means the figure refers to data that
                        no longer exists.
  --limit LIMIT         Only process the first N rows (for a trial run).
  --max-cost USD        Stop once this run's own spend (domain judge plus sentiment scorer, live
                        calls only: replies replayed from the cache cost nothing) passes USD. No
                        new comment is started; those already in flight finish, so the final
                        figure can be a little over. What is done is written, and the run exits
                        non-zero with a message. Re-run the same command to continue (the cache
                        supplies everything already answered); the cap applies to each run
                        separately. Default: no cap.
  --project-to N        after the run, print how long N comments would take at this run's speed
                        (repeatable). Default: 693 and 83,532 comments (the gold set and the
                        batching corpus; see DEFAULT_PROJECTIONS).
  --sentiment SENTIMENT
                        'vader', or 'llm:<judge spec>' e.g. 'llm:anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5'.
                        Whichever arm won evaluate.py sentiment. Available: combined, llm, stub,
                        vader
  --output OUTPUT       CSV file to write to, with the same Windows-safe encoding the collectors
                        use. If omitted, writes to stdout — fine in Git Bash, but PowerShell's '>'
                        redirection still re-encodes as UTF-16, so prefer --output there.

instrument switches (defaults reproduce the current wording):
  --fixed-examples FILE
                        CSV (comment_id, body, label) of the examples shown to the model in the
                        `fixed` arm, instead of the built-in synthetic set. For real hand-coded
                        gold comments: keep the file in a gitignored folder. They are left out of
                        scoring automatically (each would be scored against its own label), and
                        run records and the dashboard codebook hold their ids and a hash, never
                        their text.
  --story-rules {on,off}
                        off = story context is factual only, with no stance rules
  --stance-object {conduct,wealth}
                        wealth = anchor 4 is about extreme wealth and those who hold it
  --sentiment-examples {on,off}
                        off = the sentiment prompt shows no worked examples. With --fixed-examples
                        FILE holding `sentiment` and `story` columns, on (default) shows the same
                        fixed examples with their ratings
  --domain-context {facts,none}
                        none = the domain prompt carries no story background (the earlier
                        wording); facts (default) = it ends with the story's factual paragraph,
                        never the stance rules
  --combined-domain-context {keep,remove}
                        remove = the combined arm's domain question does not see the story context
```

## `slens-keywords`

Deterministic harm-domain classifier, as a check on the LLM labels.

```text
usage: slens-keywords [-h] [--keywords KEYWORDS] [--audit] [--min-hits MIN_HITS] [--output OUTPUT]
                      input_csv

positional arguments:
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --keywords KEYWORDS  Vocabulary file. Defaults to the copy shipped with the package.
  --audit              Report each term's in-category vs out-of-category match rate instead of
                       classifying. See #13.
  --min-hits MIN_HITS  Minimum total matches before a term's rate is judged (--audit only)
  --output OUTPUT      CSV file to write to, with the same Windows-safe encoding the collectors
                       use. If omitted, writes to stdout — fine in Git Bash, but PowerShell's '>'
                       redirection still re-encodes as UTF-16, so prefer --output there.
```

## `slens-evaluate`

Score classifier arms against a hand-coded gold set and print the scorecard.

```text
usage: slens-evaluate [-h] [--judge JUDGE] [--arm ARM] [--pool POOL] [--selector SELECTOR]
                      [--allow-non-fixed] [--k K] [--votes VOTES] [--concurrency CONCURRENCY]
                      [--label-column LABEL_COLUMN] [--cache CACHE]
                      [--pool-fraction POOL_FRACTION] [--out-prefix OUT_PREFIX] [--seed SEED]
                      [--exclude-ids EXCLUDE_IDS] [--bootstrap N] [--split-by {comment,video}]
                      [--fixed-examples FILE] [--story-rules {on,off}]
                      [--stance-object {conduct,wealth}] [--sentiment-examples {on,off}]
                      [--domain-context {facts,none}] [--combined-domain-context {keep,remove}]
                      {split,score,scorecard,sentiment} input_csv

positional arguments:
  {split,score,scorecard,sentiment}
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --judge JUDGE         score only. One of: anthropic, combined, gemma, google, keyword, manual,
                        ollama, openai, stub
  --arm ARM             scorecard only, repeatable: '<judge>/<selector>'
  --pool POOL           Hand-coded CSV used as the retrieval pool
  --selector SELECTOR   Default selector when an arm omits one: fixed, fixed_random, none,
                        retrieved
  --allow-non-fixed     scorecard only: permit an arm whose selector is not `fixed`. Benchmark
                        comparisons use the 25 fixed examples for every arm; this is for
                        exploratory runs outside that comparison.
  --k K                 Examples to retrieve
  --votes VOTES
  --concurrency CONCURRENCY
                        scorecard, sentiment and score: how many comments to label at once
                        (default 1, as before). An API arm spends its time waiting on the network,
                        so this turns a scorecard measured in hours into one measured in minutes;
                        the results are identical, only the clock changes. Local (Ollama or Gemma)
                        arms always run at 1. Stay well inside your provider's rate limits (check
                        the Limits page first).
  --label-column LABEL_COLUMN
  --cache CACHE         JSONL response cache; makes a rerun free and exact
  --pool-fraction POOL_FRACTION
                        split only
  --out-prefix OUT_PREFIX
                        split only: writes <prefix>_pool.csv and <prefix>_heldout.csv
  --seed SEED
  --exclude-ids EXCLUDE_IDS
                        scorecard, sentiment, split: a file of comment_ids (one per line, or a CSV
                        with a comment_id column) to leave out of scoring -- the gold comments
                        shown to the model as worked examples, which would otherwise be scored
                        against their own labels.
  --bootstrap N         scorecard only: also print 95% intervals on each category's precision,
                        recall and F1, from N resamples of whole videos (try 1000). Off by
                        default.
  --split-by {comment,video}
                        split only: 'video' keeps every video's comments on one side, so the pool
                        and held-out set share no thread (the default, 'comment', is the original
                        behaviour).

instrument switches (defaults reproduce the current wording):
  --fixed-examples FILE
                        CSV (comment_id, body, label) of the examples shown to the model in the
                        `fixed` arm, instead of the built-in synthetic set. For real hand-coded
                        gold comments: keep the file in a gitignored folder. They are left out of
                        scoring automatically (each would be scored against its own label), and
                        run records and the dashboard codebook hold their ids and a hash, never
                        their text.
  --story-rules {on,off}
                        off = story context is factual only, with no stance rules
  --stance-object {conduct,wealth}
                        wealth = anchor 4 is about extreme wealth and those who hold it
  --sentiment-examples {on,off}
                        off = the sentiment prompt shows no worked examples. With --fixed-examples
                        FILE holding `sentiment` and `story` columns, on (default) shows the same
                        fixed examples with their ratings
  --domain-context {facts,none}
                        none = the domain prompt carries no story background (the earlier
                        wording); facts (default) = it ends with the story's factual paragraph,
                        never the stance rules
  --combined-domain-context {keep,remove}
                        remove = the combined arm's domain question does not see the story context
```

## `slens-agreement`

Pairwise kappa and Krippendorff's alpha between models and the hand codes, on the gold set (counts and statistics only).

```text
usage: slens-agreement [-h] --model NAME=FILE [--no-gold] [--bootstrap BOOTSTRAP]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model NAME=FILE     a labelled gold CSV for one model (repeat for each model)
  --no-gold             leave the hand codes out and compare only the models
  --bootstrap BOOTSTRAP
                        resamples for the interval
```

## `slens-validate`

Compare harm labels across methods and draw a hand-coding sample.

```text
usage: slens-validate [-h] [--coders CODERS [CODERS ...]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--master MASTER]
                      [--replacements REPLACEMENTS] [--topup TOPUP]
                      [--sentiment-agreement {exact,bucket}] [--adjudicated ADJUDICATED]
                      [--corpus CORPUS] [--json-output JSON_OUTPUT] [--second-input SECOND_INPUT]
                      [--sentiment-levels {scale,buckets}]
                      [--extra-inputs EXTRA_INPUTS [EXTRA_INPUTS ...]] [--exclude-ids EXCLUDE_IDS]
                      [--allow-partial] [--no-example-exclusion] [--core-ids CORE_IDS]
                      [--compare-json COMPARE_JSON] [--labelled LABELLED] [--n N] [--seed SEED]
                      [--stratify-by STRATIFY_BY] [--output OUTPUT]
                      [--video-cap-fraction VIDEO_CAP_FRACTION]
                      {agree,sample,score,join,interrater,combine,selfconsistency,reweight}
                      [input_csv]

positional arguments:
  {agree,sample,score,join,interrater,combine,selfconsistency,reweight}
  input_csv             For `interrater`: the first coder's completed file. Not used by `combine`
                        -- see --coders/--manifest/--master instead.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --coders CODERS [CODERS ...]
                        `combine` only: every coder's completed file (.xlsx or .csv).
  --manifest MANIFEST   `combine` only: scripts_scratch_split_gold_set.py's manifest (comment_id,
                        assigned_to, is_core), recording who coded what.
  --master MASTER       `combine` and `reweight`: the drawn gold sample (e.g.
                        gold_sample_balanced.csv) -- inclusion_prob always comes from here, never
                        from a coder's own (possibly stale) copy of it.
  --replacements REPLACEMENTS
                        `combine` only, optional: a hand-coded file of comments that replace
                        specific drawn rows (e.g. because their video was later excluded), each
                        row carrying a replaces_comment_id column naming which drawn row it stands
                        in for.
  --topup TOPUP         `combine` and `reweight`, optional: a later random draw of extra comments
                        from each story's unclassified stratum (e.g. gold_sample_topup.csv). Needs
                        no split-manifest entry; whoever coded it, in --coders, is used.
  --sentiment-agreement {exact,bucket}
                        `combine` only: when two coders rated the same core comment, 'exact' needs
                        identical sentiment; 'bucket' accepts the same side (1-2 negative, 3
                        neutral, 4-5 positive; 0 and -1 stay exact) and writes the bucket word.
  --adjudicated ADJUDICATED
                        `combine` only, optional: a file of comment_id, hand_domain,
                        hand_sentiment resolving rows the coders disagreed on. Each overrides the
                        coders' answers for that comment.
  --corpus CORPUS       `combine` and `reweight`: the FINAL corpus with a primary_category column
                        (e.g. the *_kw_primary.csv). When given, every inclusion probability is
                        recomputed against it, instead of copied from the sample files, which
                        describe the frame as it was when drawn. Requires --video-cap-fraction (0
                        for none).
  --json-output JSON_OUTPUT
                        Write `interrater`'s figures as JSON, for the dashboard. Coder agreement
                        is the ceiling on every accuracy claim in the project; if it can only be
                        retyped from a terminal it stops being evidence.
  --second-input SECOND_INPUT
                        `interrater` only: the second coder's completed file, covering the same
                        comment_ids as input_csv.
  --sentiment-levels {scale,buckets}
                        `interrater` with three or more coders: how the stance is compared.
                        'scale' (default) compares the 1-5 ratings (ordinal alpha); 'buckets'
                        compares only the direction, 1-2 negative / 3 neutral / 4-5 positive, as
                        three ordered classes. The kind-of-answer figure (stance / irrelevant /
                        uncodeable) is reported either way.
  --extra-inputs EXTRA_INPUTS [EXTRA_INPUTS ...]
                        `interrater` only, optional: any THIRD or later coder's completed file(s),
                        for more than two overlapping coders (e.g. the shared 50-row core coded by
                        all 5). Passing this switches the report from pairwise Cohen's kappa to
                        Fleiss' kappa across every file given (input_csv + --second-input +
                        --extra-inputs).
  --exclude-ids EXCLUDE_IDS
                        `score` only: a file of comment_ids (one per line, or a CSV with a
                        comment_id column) to leave out of scoring -- the comments shown to the
                        model as worked examples.
  --allow-partial       `join` only: accept a join in which some coded comments are not in
                        --labelled. They are written without machine labels and every scorer then
                        leaves them out (counted), never scores them as misses. Without this flag
                        such a join is refused.
  --no-example-exclusion
                        `score` only: silence the warning printed when no worked-example ids are
                        known (no run record beside the file and no --exclude-ids). Use it only
                        when none of the gold comments was shown to the model as an example.
  --core-ids CORE_IDS   `selfconsistency` only: a file naming the comment_ids to restrict to (one
                        per line, or any CSV with a comment_id column) -- e.g. official-
                        data/gold_sample_core_50.csv, so this measures the LLM's self-consistency
                        on the SAME comments the human coder-vs-coder kappa was measured on, not a
                        different, much larger set that isn't a fair comparison. Omit to measure
                        over every row in input_csv instead.
  --compare-json COMPARE_JSON
                        `selfconsistency` only: a prior `slens-validate interrater --json-output
                        ...` run's file, printed alongside this run's figures for a direct side-
                        by-side instead of two outputs to reconcile by eye.
  --labelled LABELLED   `join` only: the labelled corpus to take the machine labels from, matched
                        on comment_id. `sample` strips those columns so the coder cannot see the
                        machine's answer; `join` puts them back afterwards, which is what `score`
                        and --scored need.
  --n N                 Sample size for `sample`
  --seed SEED
  --stratify-by STRATIFY_BY
                        Column(s) to stratify `sample` on instead of story+platform, comma-
                        separated, e.g. kw_domain or story,kw_domain. A domain column over-samples
                        rare categories so they can be validated (#18); adding story alongside it
                        also keeps one story from dominating a category's examples.
  --output OUTPUT       Write `sample`'s CSV directly to this file, with the same Windows-safe
                        encoding the collectors use. If omitted, writes to stdout — fine in Git
                        Bash, but PowerShell's '>' redirection still re-encodes as UTF-16, so
                        prefer --output there.
  --video-cap-fraction VIDEO_CAP_FRACTION
                        `sample` and `combine --corpus`: cap how much of a stratum's allocation
                        can come from one video, as a fraction (e.g. 0.15 = at most 15%). A soft
                        cap -- if a stratum cannot reach its target within the cap, the shortfall
                        is backfilled past it rather than under-filling the stratum. Guards
                        against a story's gold sample being mostly one or two videos' comments,
                        which understates the between-video variance the clustered bootstrap
                        depends on. Omit for the old uncapped behaviour.
```

## `slens-report`

Confidence intervals for classified proportions, via bootstrap resampling.

```text
usage: slens-report [-h] [--strict-corpus] --column COLUMN [--by BY] [--cluster-by CLUSTER_BY]
                    [--tpr TPR] [--fpr FPR] [--base {all,classified,both}]
                    [--rescale-unclassified FROZEN_CORPUS] [--exclude-ids FILE]
                    [--no-example-exclusion] [--n-boot N_BOOT] [--seed SEED] [--gold GOLD]
                    [--gold-label-column GOLD_LABEL_COLUMN] [--category CATEGORY]
                    [--min-genuine-positives MIN_GENUINE_POSITIVES]
                    [--max-discard-fraction MAX_DISCARD_FRACTION]
                    [--min-gold-clusters MIN_GOLD_CLUSTERS]
                    {observed,aggregate,corrected,corrected-bootstrap,ppi-bootstrap,corrected-by-story}
                    input_csv

positional arguments:
  {observed,aggregate,corrected,corrected-bootstrap,ppi-bootstrap,corrected-by-story}
  input_csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --strict-corpus       Refuse to run if the corpus no longer matches its manifest. These are the
                        figures that reach the paper, so this is the command most worth setting it
                        on.
  --column COLUMN       Binary/numeric column, e.g. domain_democracy or sentiment_value
  --by BY               Group-by column for 'observed'
  --cluster-by CLUSTER_BY
                        Resampling unit column (default: source, i.e. video)
  --tpr TPR             corrected: recall from the gold set
  --fpr FPR             corrected: false positive rate from the gold set
  --base {all,classified,both}
                        Which denominator the share is over. 'all' (default, as before): every
                        answered comment, including those the classifier tagged with no harm.
                        'classified': only comments tagged with at least one harm. 'both': print
                        the two side by side. The gold rows are restricted to the same base for
                        any corrected figure.
  --rescale-unclassified FROZEN_CORPUS
                        corrected-bootstrap/ppi-bootstrap/corrected-by-story: a SENSITIVITY run.
                        Scale the gold weights of each story's unclassified strata so they sum to
                        that stratum's size in FROZEN_CORPUS (a corpus with story and
                        primary_category, e.g. the frozen master). Run it beside the same command
                        without the flag and report both; it is not a correction and does not
                        explain why the stored weights are short.
  --exclude-ids FILE    corrected-bootstrap/ppi-bootstrap/corrected-by-story: leave these gold
                        comments out (a CSV with a comment_id column; the --fixed-examples file
                        works). Comments shown to the model as worked examples must not feed the
                        correction: each would be scored against its own answer.
  --no-example-exclusion
                        corrected-bootstrap/ppi-bootstrap/corrected-by-story: silence the warning
                        printed when no worked-example ids are known (no run record beside --gold,
                        no --exclude-ids). Use it only when none of the gold comments was shown to
                        the model as an example.
  --n-boot N_BOOT
  --seed SEED
  --gold GOLD           corrected-bootstrap: a gold CSV carrying both the machine labels
                        (domain_*) and the hand codes -- i.e. one that has been through slens-
                        classify, not the blind file slens-validate sample produces
  --gold-label-column GOLD_LABEL_COLUMN
                        corrected-bootstrap: the hand-coded column in --gold (default hand_domain)
  --category CATEGORY   corrected-bootstrap: the harm category, e.g. democracy. Defaults to
                        --column with a leading 'domain_' stripped, when --column is shaped that
                        way (domain_democracy -> democracy)
  --min-genuine-positives MIN_GENUINE_POSITIVES
                        corrected-bootstrap/ppi-bootstrap: refuse below this many EFFECTIVE
                        (Horvitz-Thompson-weighted, Kish-style) genuine positives in --gold
                        (default 10; figures under 50 are flagged LOW EVIDENCE), not a raw row
                        count -- see weighted_effective_positive_count's docstring for why a raw
                        count overstates how much a stratified gold set actually supports
  --max-discard-fraction MAX_DISCARD_FRACTION
                        corrected-bootstrap: refuse rather than report if more than this share of
                        bootstrap iterations go degenerate (default 0.05)
  --min-gold-clusters MIN_GOLD_CLUSTERS
                        corrected-bootstrap: refuse if --gold has fewer distinct --cluster-by
                        values than this (default 2) -- one cluster resamples to itself and would
                        report a zero-width interval
```

## `slens-export-dashboard`

Build the single JSON file the QA dashboard reads.

```text
usage: slens-export-dashboard [-h] --output OUTPUT [--exclude-ids FILE] [--scored SCORED]
                              [--exclusions EXCLUSIONS] [--video-list VIDEO_LIST]
                              [--interrater INTERRATER] [--cluster-by CLUSTER_BY]
                              [--n-boot N_BOOT] [--allow-unvalidated] [--run-record FILE]
                              [--allow-instrument-mismatch] [--corpus CORPUS] [--include-verbatim]
                              [--status {provisional,validated}]
                              labelled_csv

positional arguments:
  labelled_csv          A corpus that has been through slens-classify

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT       Where to write results.json
  --exclude-ids FILE    Leave these gold comments out of the validation figures (a CSV with a
                        comment_id column, e.g. the --fixed-examples file). The comments the run
                        record lists as fixed examples are left out automatically.
  --scored SCORED       Hand-coded rows joined to their machine labels, for the validation tab
  --exclusions EXCLUSIONS
                        The exclusion table slens-collect wrote
  --video-list VIDEO_LIST
                        The video list slens-collect wrote
  --interrater INTERRATER
                        JSON from a coder-agreement run, if you have one
  --cluster-by CLUSTER_BY
                        Column identifying the cluster. Leave as `source` (the video): clustering
                        by anything finer understates every interval.
  --n-boot N_BOOT
  --allow-unvalidated   Write even with no hand-coded scores. The dashboard then says so on every
                        tab -- these are the numbers of a classifier nobody has checked, which is
                        not the same as a result.
  --run-record FILE     The run record (.run.json) for the labelled file, when it is not at
                        <labelled_csv>.run.json -- e.g. after the file was renamed. slens-keywords
                        copies the record beside its output, so the classify -> keywords -> export
                        chain finds it without this.
  --allow-instrument-mismatch
                        Export even when the gold file's run record shows it was labelled by a
                        different judge, scorer, prompt, example set or switch than the corpus.
                        The validation figures then describe a different classifier from the one
                        that labelled the corpus; the mismatch is recorded in provenance.
  --corpus CORPUS       The frozen corpus the labels came from. Checked against the hash in the
                        run record beside the labelled file; the export is refused if they differ.
  --include-verbatim    Put real comment text in results.json: the worked examples and the
                        machine-versus-human disagreement table. OFF by default, so a published
                        export quotes no one; a verbatim comment can be searched for and traced to
                        its author.
  --status {provisional,validated}
                        Stamped on the dashboard. `validated` needs --scored.
```
